nodes.description: Constitutive SERCA1 loss produces marked reduction in calcium transport, neonatal diaphragm dysfunction and death shortly after birth. The model captures severe loss of pump function but not the usually survivable human course. Diaphragm fibre composition, species-specific adaptation and residual allele activity may contribute to the mismatch.

Biallelic pathogenic variants reduce SERCA1 abundance, stability or intrinsic calcium-transport function. Truncating alleles, exon/gene deletions, splice changes, in-frame deletions and missense substitutions are reported. Mechanisms overlap and cannot be assigned solely from variant class; for example, a splice variant causes an in-frame exon skip.

nodes.description: Muscle explants preserve differentiated diseased tissue for MG132 or corrector exposure. C17 and C4 increased mutant SERCA1 in SR-enriched fractions. Ex vivo response avoids whole-animal pharmacokinetics and therefore cannot establish systemic safety or functional benefit.

C17, C4 and C9 increase abundance of selected bovine SERCA1 mutants in heterologous cells. Local C17 injections in two affected calves increased SR-associated SERCA1 and calcium-ATPase activity; whole-animal functional recovery and systemic safety were not established. C17 failed to improve key morphological and locomotor outcomes in the S766F accordion zebrafish model, which has a different molecular defect. Lumacaftor and tezacaftor were relatively ineffective in the tested cell assay. Human therapeutic benefit remains unproven.
